ai.title: Enforce CLI login for anonymous users
ai.summary: CLI startup now blocks anonymous sessions, forcing `client.login()` before prompt rendering if no user exists. Login code expiration extended from 5 minutes to 1 hour in `websocket-action.ts` to accommodate this flow. `displayGreeting` moved to `menu.ts`, consolidating cost mode and git warnings for authenticated users only. Logout logic in `client.ts` wrapped in try/catch to prevent crashes when credentials file is missing.

eli5.text: The command-line tool now requires you to log in before it will let you start a session, so if you open it without signing in first, it will stop you and ask you to do that. While you're doing this, the login code you receive will stay valid for an hour instead of just five minutes, giving you plenty of time to enter it. Before anything appears on your screen, the tool will show you whether you are logged in and remind you about your project's settings. This applies to you whenever you start the tool; if you aren't already signed in, you have to sign in before you can use it.

ai.title: Lite mode runs non-obvious file request
ai.summary: requestRelevantFiles in backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts now always issues the non-obvious file request, removing the `costMode !== 'lite'` gate. Lite mode `countPerRequest` raised from 7 to 8 to match standard. Prompt text consolidated into explicit exclusion lists for test files and `knowledge.md`.

eli5.text: The assistant now searches for the same helpful files whether you use the fast, cheap version or the regular version, previously it only did this deeper search for the regular version. If you were using the lite version, you may now see a few more relevant files suggested than before, since it now pulls in 8 files instead of 7. Behind the scenes, the rules for what files to skip were also rewritten to be clearer about excluding test files and internal documentation.

ai.title: Restore cursor on exit and hide during loading
ai.summary: Added cursor visibility management to CLI. Hides cursor via ANSI escape `\u001B[?25l` during "Thinking..." spinner and restores it via `\u001B[?25h` on exit, SIGTERM, or animation stop. Prevents terminal from remaining without cursor after interruption. Updates `npm-app/src/cli.ts` and documents behavior in `npm-app/knowledge.md`.

eli5.text: If you run the tool in a terminal, your text cursor will now hide while the assistant is thinking and reappear reliably when the program exits or stops. This prevents the cursor from staying invisible if the program is interrupted, so your terminal prompt stays usable.
